subject.title: [Bug] Sandbox validateEnvVarValue base64 heuristic false-positives on legitimate long alphanumeric values

question: Should OpenClaw narrow the sandbox env credential-data warning to structured base64 values only when the env var name also looks credential-related?
rationale: The false positive is source-reproducible, but reducing advisory credential-warning coverage is a sandbox/security policy choice rather than a purely mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Approve key-aware warning policy
options.body: Refresh the linked PR onto current main, port the active skill runtime caller, and land after sandbox/security review.

options.title: Preserve broader warning coverage
options.body: Keep the issue open and ask for a different heuristic that reduces false positives without relying on credential-looking names.

options.title: Close as intentional policy
options.body: If broad warnings are preferred for sandbox safety, document that policy and close the report as intentional behavior.

recommendation.title: Approve key-aware warning policy
recommendation.body: Refresh the linked PR onto current main, port the active skill runtime caller, and land after sandbox/security review.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the sanitizer warning behavior and are the strongest history-backed routing candidate for this security tradeoff.
